_comment: Read by fill.py on every run, and by `fill.py --check` in CI. `keep` terms come back verbatim, case-sensitive: product and brand names (Duct's own included: Content Studio, the Duct Doctrine, the maker's Ship with AI channel), vendors, the mosaic inscriptions, acronyms. A common word that only sometimes names a brand (Threads, Make, X) does not belong here, because the check cannot tell the two apart; `terms` pin one rendering per language so the same concept never gets two words; `register` is how each language addresses the reader.

brief.note: The weekly synthesis Duct writes. A noun.

desk.note: The screen a brief opens on.

change set.note: A proposed, previewable batch of edits to an ad account or property.

toolbox.note: The page where every connector and MCP server is added; called Connections until November 2026.

project.note: One client or product; the unit everything is scoped to.

post.note: A social post draft. Never the verb.

memory.note: What Duct remembers about a project across runs.

artifact.note: A versioned document an agent produced.

agent.note: An AI agent: Duct's own, or the person's coding agent. Never 代理, which reads as a proxy or a sales agency.

apply.note: Push an approved change set to the live account.

register.es: Informal (tú), never usted. Neutral Spanish readable in Spain and Latin America: avoid regional slang. Sentence case; no exclamation marks the English does not have.
register.pt-BR: Brazilian Portuguese, informal (você). Sentence case. Prefer the plain verb to a nominalisation.
register.de: Informal (du), the register of Slack, Notion and Linear in German. Sentence case; nouns capitalised as German requires. Prefer short compound-free phrasing where the English is short: a button label must stay a button label.
register.ja: Polite form (です・ます) throughout, as a professional SaaS product speaks. No honorific inflation (no ございます). Use カタカナ for established SaaS loanwords rather than inventing kanji terms. Keep button labels to a verb or a noun, never a full sentence.
register.zh-CN: Simplified Chinese for mainland China, as modern developer tools write it (GitHub, Vercel, Cursor in Chinese): address the reader as 你, never 您. Plain and direct; no marketing exaggeration (no 极致, 赋能, 一站式). Full-width Chinese punctuation (，。：？！“”); one half-width space between Chinese and Latin letters or numbers ("连接 GA4 后", "3 个连接器"). Arabic numerals. Keep button labels to a verb or a short noun phrase, never a full sentence.
